method.keyframes: All 24 keyframes inspected via three contact sheets.
method.entireTimeline: All seven full-duration sheet pages opened, with one-second samples from 0 to 204.5 seconds.
method.motion: Compared actual positions and actions across one-second samples for three moving clips; this is not continuous playback or a frame-by-frame review.

overall: Two observed visual issues require selected-shot repair; no further material semantic blockers found in the opened frames.

reviews.observation: Filled cart and hook question are visible. The scene supplies shopping context without claiming the subject bought outside a plan.
The price-board sentence now shows the sale shelf directly, correcting the prior semantic delay.
Actual offer labels remain clear beside checkout context. The headline previews unit price versus total; the later original graphic supplies the explicit comparison.
People walk and browse in the real clip across samples. It remains illustrative trip context, not evidence of a particular local store.
The caveat is readable in a clean split, with the shopper face and basket visible. It attributes no negative behavior to this subject.
The kitchen source is dark and the lower gradient adds darkness. The open fridge, raised hand and contents remain recognizable. Brightness could be tuned in a future aesthetic pass.
The whole original prompt graphic is readable; its footer says it is illustrative. Captions leave the important rows clear.
The phone and shopper are visible. Narration does not misidentify the unreadable phone content.
The diptych retains carton variety and the yellow offer label. Headline and captions do not cover the key label.
The hand reaches and handles products across the 63.5–70.5 second samples. This illustrates a product encounter; it does not establish the actor’s private intention.
The fridge portrait and cart remain readable with the question overlay. Private intention is not proven; the spoken text offers alternative interpretations.
The native 1080p label now separates stock illustration and Inman 2009 research. It does not imply this stock image depicts the study.
The plum display and bright price card are visible. The caveat attributes no specific behavior to a depicted person.
The actual multiple-unit offer is visible before the original hypothetical comparison. No local price claim is made.
The full graphic preserves one versus two boxes, 30k versus 50k total, 30k versus 25k unit price and the hypothetical header. Captions do not cover the main numbers.
The full graphic now says additional spending 20k and preserves the 30k/50k comparison. Arithmetic is visible.
Cover crop removes the one-box 30k side and part of the hypothetical header in the left pane, so the comparison is incomplete. Root is preparing explicit contain behavior.
A filled basket is depicted while narration correctly says the basket alone cannot establish waste.

The gallery right card shows 50k and the additional 20k at native 1080p. The left comparison is partly occluded by the central card, so it functions as a callback rather than the first full explanation.
Actual unloading and cashier handling progress across 156.5–165.5 second samples. Advice uses questions about a possible decision; no claim that payment is visible.
The portrait retains both faces and checkout equipment with blurred side fill. The static reflective beat lasts about 11 seconds; it is context, not proof of intention.
The large headline overlaps the third checklist row. Root is preparing explicit contain behavior and removing this headline.
Home groceries supply context without a false before/after claim. Caption and narration offer possible interpretations.
CTA headline and short body are clear. Face and basket remain visible, although the top of the head is cropped. The final spoken caption remains through the ending.

limits: This is not aesthetic acceptance on behalf of the user.
A successful decode was not used as visual-quality proof.
The unchanged research claim remains scoped to the study abstract; no new primary fact verification was performed in this render review.
